content: Clinical judgment is essential when deciding whether to initiate tuberculosis (TB) treatment. All patients diagnosed with bacterial or Pneumocystis infections must complete the full course of treatment. For hospitalized people living with HIV (PLHIV) being evaluated for TB who do not exhibit TB symptoms but are seriously ill, have advanced HIV disease (AHD), or a CD4 count below 200 cells/mm³, the following steps should be taken: 1. Collect a urine sample and perform the lateral flow lipoarabinomannan assay (LF-LAM) test. If the LF-LAM test is negative and the CD4 count is below 200 cells/mm³, reevaluate the patient and conduct additional testing as per national guidelines. If the LF-LAM test is negative and the CD4 count is above 200 cells/mm³, provide an AHD package of care. If the LF-LAM test is positive, initiate TB treatment based on the result and clinical judgment. Additionally, collect a specimen for molecular testing (mWRD) to assess rifampicin resistance. If the mWRD result indicates MTB complex detected, follow the appropriate algorithm for interpretation, further testing, and treatment recommendations. Conduct culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (DST) to evaluate drug resistance. For hospitalized PLHIV without TB symptoms and with a CD4 count of 200 cells/mm³ or higher (or unknown CD4 count), do not perform the LF-LAM test. Instead, manage the patient clinically. For PLHIV being evaluated for TB who present with TB symptoms or are seriously ill: 1. Collect a urine sample for LF-LAM testing and a specimen for mWRD testing. If mWRD is available on-site, perform it in parallel with LF-LAM testing. For pulmonary TB evaluation, use induced or expectorated sputum (preferred), bronchoalveolar lavage, gastric lavage, or nasopharyngeal aspirate. Stool samples may also be used for Xpert MTB/RIF testing. For extrapulmonary TB evaluation, use cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), lymph node aspirates, pleural fluid, or other relevant samples for Xpert MTB testing. Blood samples may be used for disseminated TB in HIV-positive individuals. If the LF-LAM test is positive, initiate TB treatment immediately while awaiting mWRD results. Follow the appropriate algorithm for interpreting mWRD results, including drug resistance detection, and adjust therapy as needed. If the LF-LAM test is negative, TB is not ruled out. Evaluate mWRD results and conduct further testing as per national guidelines. For PLHIV without TB symptoms or serious illness: 1. Assess CD4 count and AHD status. If the CD4 count is below 100 cells/mm³ or the patient has a WHO stage 3 or 4 event, perform LF-LAM testing. If positive, initiate TB treatment and conduct drug resistance testing. If negative, provide an AHD package of care. If the CD4 count is between 100–200 cells/mm³, do not perform LF-LAM testing; instead, provide an AHD package of care. If the CD4 count is above 200 cells/mm³ or unknown, manage the patient clinically without LF-LAM testing. For patients with rifampicin-resistant (RR-TB) or multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB), WHO recommends initiating treatment promptly with a shorter all-oral bedaquiline-containing regimen lasting 9–12 months, if eligible. Molecular and phenotypic DST should be performed to guide treatment decisions. If resistance to fluoroquinolones (FQs) is detected, place the patient on an individualized longer regimen based on WHO priority grouping of medicines. If no resistance is detected, continue the shorter regimen while awaiting phenotypic DST results. Phenotypic DST should be conducted for all drugs included in the treatment regimen, such as bedaquiline, linezolid, and clofazimine, where reliable methods are available. Treatment should not be delayed while awaiting DST results. Monthly monitoring and close follow-up are essential to assess treatment response and adjust regimens as needed.
